title: Orsen and the Well
premise: Xanthe Joubert hosts a graveyard-shift radio show where the callers are all people who died within the past week, and he keeps meticulous logs because writing things down is the only ritual that keeps him sane. When photographs from his late grandmother's house begin showing an extra chair in every frame, he realizes the Well beneath the family property is counting residents, and it intends to collect. His grandmother, still alive but fading, is the last resident who can sign the deed that transfers the debt to whoever holds the papers next. Xanthe must move his family out ahead of the count and destroy the inheritance before his grandmother signs—or before the chair fills with someone he loves.
about_author: Elodie Ishikawa is a former overnight radio producer from Marseille who now writes horror in a converted lighthouse keeper's cottage on the Breton coast. She claims she has never answered a phone after 3 a.m., on principle.

chapters.title: Dead Air
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. On his shift at KRVL, Xanthe takes a call from a listener whose obituary ran three days ago; her voice is warm, grateful, and wrong. He logs the call in his notebook as always. The emotional beat is quiet dread: the routine that comforts him has just cracked open.

chapters.title: The Estate Inventory
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Returning to grandma Odile's house to sort her affairs, Xanthe catalogs belongings for the lawyer and finds a ledger of names going back six generations—each entry dated, each name crossed out on the same date. Beat: unease hardening into suspicion.

chapters.title: An Extra Chair
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Comparing old family photos against new ones taken the same afternoon, Xanthe counts chairs: every image now includes one more—a plain wooden chair facing the camera. Beat: the horror becomes visual and undeniable.

chapters.title: Callers
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Xanthe and his sister Marguerite. Marguerite calls the show anonymously to describe a dream of sitting in a chair underground; Xanthe recognizes her voice and says nothing on air. Beat: love and concealment beginning to strain against each other.

chapters.title: The Well Beneath
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Following the ledger's oldest map notation, Xanthe finds a capped stone well behind the collapsed greenhouse, its cover chained and warm to the touch despite October frost. Beat: physical confrontation with the source.

chapters.title: Odile Remembers
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The grandmother, lucid for the first time in months, tells Xanthe about the arrangement her own mother made: the Well keeps the family safe and solvent, and in exchange it counts them, one by one, until the papers pass to a new signer. Beat: inheritance revealed as predation.

chapters.title: Documentation Is a Kind of Prayer
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe transcribes decades of Odile's records and discovers the crossed-out names correspond exactly to the dead callers on his show—the Well broadcasts through him. Beat: guilt; he has been the Well's mouthpiece without knowing.

chapters.title: Marguerite Comes Home
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Against Xanthe's warnings, Marguerite moves into the house with her daughter Sylvie to help care for Odile. That night she dreams of the chair again, closer. Beat: duty pulling the family toward the count.

chapters.title: The Lawyer's Papers
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The estate lawyer arrives with transfer documents; Odile's signature would make Xanthe the next resident of record. Xanthe hides the papers and lies to everyone about why. Beat: deception as an act of protection.

chapters.title: Voices in Rotation
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. On air, the dead callers stop being gentle. They recite the Joubert family tree, name by name, ending with Sylvie's. Beat: escalation—the Well has moved from haunting to threat.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Cost
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A flashback chapter: 1968, young Odile watching her mother sign, learning what 'safe and solvent' purchased—the neighbors' misfortunes, the uncle who vanished. Beat: sympathy deepens; Odile is both victim and accomplice.

chapters.title: Sylvie Draws the Chair
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Seven-year-old Sylvie draws the wooden chair at school, with a figure in it, and labels it with a name no one taught her: Xanthe. Beat: terror turns intimate; the count has chosen.

chapters.title: Eviction Notice
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe tries to move the family out, but roads loop back to the house; the town itself seems to hold them. Marguerite accuses him of losing his mind. Beat: isolation—the price of carrying the secret alone.

chapters.title: The Chain
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe breaks the chain on the well cap and looks down: not water but rows of chairs descending into dark, most occupied by shapes wearing family faces. One chair is empty. Beat: the count made literal.

chapters.title: Confession on Air
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Live, at 3 a.m., Xanthe abandons the format and confesses everything to his listeners—including the dead ones—and asks them how to break a contract signed by the dead. One voice answers: let the last resident refuse. Beat: desperate hope.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Xanthe asks Odile to refuse to sign, ever, even as the Well begins taking payment early—her strength, her memories draining nightly. She agrees, knowing refusal may kill her faster than signing. Beat: love against duty, both directions.

chapters.title: The Count Advances
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The house begins rearranging itself around the extra chair; doors open onto the well shaft. Marguerite finally believes Xanthe, and they work together to get Sylvie out—but the car won't start until dawn, when the count resets. Beat: alliance forged under siege.

chapters.title: Signing Ceremony
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The lawyer returns flanked by the dead callers, papers in hand, insisting the estate cannot close unsigned. Odile, barely conscious, reaches for the pen. Beat: climax pressure at maximum.

chapters.title: The Empty Chair
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. To stop the signing, Xanthe sits in the extra chair himself and offers the Well a trade: his voice, his show, his name in the ledger, if the family walks free. The dead fall silent. Beat: sacrifice as climax.

chapters.title: Dawn Count
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. At sunrise the roads open. Marguerite drives Odile and Sylvie away while Xanthe stays behind, unresisting, as the well cap closes over the sound of his breathing. Beat: grief and release entwined.

chapters.title: Sign-Off
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Weeks later, KRVL's overnight slot plays static, then a familiar voice reading names—not the dead anymore, but the living, a roll call of everyone the Well released. Marguerite listens every night. Beat: mourning transformed into vigil.

chapters.title: The Last Entry
chapters.summary: Epilogue, mixed POV. In the sealed house, the ledger's final page shows Xanthe's name uncrossed, the chair in the photographs now empty and turned away. Somewhere below, a man documents everything, because documentation is a kind of prayer. Beat: ambiguous, haunted resolution.
